metadata.title: Graph Traversal: BFS vs DFS
metadata.subject: Computer Science
metadata.objective: Show the BFS and DFS visiting orders and the frontier each one uses.
misconceptions: DFS always finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph
A visited node can be visited again
BFS and DFS always produce the same order
expectedUnderstanding: BFS explores level by level with a queue, while DFS follows one branch with a stack.
The visited set grows and each node is visited exactly once.
For this graph BFS visits A, B, C, D, E and DFS visits A, B, D, E, C.

primitives.text: BFS: A  B  C  D  E
DFS: A  B  D  E  C

checkpoints.title: Begin at A
checkpoints.body: A is the only node in the frontier. A queue puts each new neighbour at the back; a stack puts it on top. That one difference decides the whole visiting order.

checkpoints.title: Visit A
checkpoints.body: A is marked visited. BFS enqueues B and C, so the whole next level waits in the queue before either child is explored.

checkpoints.title: Visit B
checkpoints.body: BFS visits B and enqueues D and E behind C, so the frontier is C, D, E. DFS would instead push D and descend into it immediately, leaving C for later.

checkpoints.title: Visit C
checkpoints.body: C adds no new nodes because B and E are already known. BFS has finished the second level, and D and E are next in the queue.

checkpoints.title: Visit D
checkpoints.body: D is visited once and adds no new nodes. E is the last node still queued.

checkpoints.title: Visit E and compare the orders
checkpoints.body: BFS finishes with A, B, C, D, E. Set the mode slider to 1 to see the DFS order A, B, D, E, C. Each node appears once, and only BFS guarantees shortest unweighted distances.

narration.text: Start at A. BFS uses a queue, so it will finish a level before going deeper.
Visit A. B and C enter the queue, in that order.
Visit B. Its unvisited neighbours D and E join the queue behind C.
Visit C. It adds no new nodes, so the frontier is D and E.
Visit D. E is the last node in the queue.
Visit E. The BFS order is A, B, C, D, E. Switch the mode slider to compare the DFS order A, B, D, E, C.

fallback.text: A graph with edges A-B, A-C, B-D, B-E and E-C. BFS uses a queue and visits A, B, C, D, E level by level. DFS uses a stack and visits A, B, D, E, C by following one branch as far as it goes. Each node is visited exactly once.

accessibility.alt: A graph with nodes A to E and edges A-B, A-C, B-D, B-E and E-C. Two rows give the BFS order A, B, C, D, E and the DFS order A, B, D, E, C. A green band marks how many nodes have been visited as the mode slider switches rows.
